docs.title: DocumentationExamples using earth2studio.utils.checkpoint.Checkpoint
docs.text:
Catalog of restart checkpoints for a named inference run.

A checkpoint owns the on-disk catalog and commit directories for one logical inference run. Each committed catalog row stores generic workflow metadata and component state bound through bind_checkpoint_state.

Parameters:

  • name (str) –

    Name of the checkpoint store. Used in the default checkpoint path and in commit manifests.

  • path (str | Path | None, default: None ) –

    Directory where checkpoint files are stored. If None, checkpoints are written under the default Earth2Studio cache location, by default None.

  • mode (Literal['overwrite', 'append'], default: 'overwrite' ) –

    Catalog update mode. "overwrite" keeps only the latest row; "append" preserves row history for repeated writes, by default "overwrite".

  • flush_interval (int | None, default: 1 ) –

    Number of workflow write calls between durable commits. Use None to keep updates pending until flush is called explicitly, by default 1.

  • history_size (int | None, default: None ) –

    Maximum number of rows to keep when mode="append". In overwrite mode this is ignored and treated as one latest row, by default None.

  • level (CheckpointLevel, default: 2 ) –

    Requested component logging level. 0 records workflow progress and explicit metadata only, 1 allows component state needed to restart workflow items such as ensemble members, and 2 allows component state needed to resume inside a forecast rollout, by default 2.

  • rank (int | None, default: None ) –

    Distributed rank for this process. If None, Earth2Studio attempts to detect the rank from PhysicsNeMo or common distributed environment variables, by default None.

  • world_size (int | None, default: None ) –

    Distributed world size. If None, Earth2Studio attempts to detect the world size from PhysicsNeMo or WORLD_SIZE, by default None.

  • device (str | device, default: device('cpu') ) –

    Device where components should stage live tensor state before it is serialized into the checkpoint, by default torch.device("cpu").

docs.title: Documentation
docs.text:
Interpolate x linearly along a vertical coordinate onto target levels.

The coordinate can be anything monotonic within a column: pressure (with log=True, for interpolation linear in log pressure), height or depth.

Parameters:

  • x (Tensor) –

    Field with a level dimension dim.

  • coordinate (Tensor) –

    Coordinate of each of x's levels: either one value per level, shape (level,) in any order without repeats, or one column per point, shaped like x (or broadcastable to it) and monotonic along dim in the same direction in every column. Columns that are not strictly monotonic, such as hybrid levels under an implausible surface pressure, are filled with fill_value, or NaN without one, rather than interpolated.

  • target (Tensor) –

    Coordinate of each output level, shape (target,), in the same units.

  • dim (int, default: -1 ) –

    Level dimension of x and coordinate, by default -1

  • log (bool, default: False ) –

    Interpolate linearly in the logarithm of the coordinate, as for pressure, by default False

  • fill_value (float | None, default: None ) –

    Value for targets outside a column's range, by default None, which takes the nearest level's value instead.

Returns:

  • Tensor –

    x with dimension dim replaced by the target levels, in x's dtype. Coordinates and weights are computed in at least single precision, as pressures in Pa overflow half precision.

docs.text:
obs_to_grid(
    obs: DataFrame | None,
    variables: list[str] | None = None,
    request_time: datetime64 | None = None,
    time_tolerance: (
        timedelta64 | tuple[timedelta64, timedelta64] | None
    ) = None,
    return_empty_grid: bool = False,
) -> tuple[Tensor, Tensor] | tuple[None, None]

Bin point observations onto the model grid.

Observations are filtered to variables and to those within time_tolerance of request_time. Multiple observations that fall in the same grid cell are averaged.

Parameters:

  • obs (DataFrame or None) –

    Observation table with columns variable, lat, lon, observation. If request_time is used, obs must also have a time column.

  • variables (list[str], default: None ) –

    Variable names to retain; others are discarded. None (default) uses all variables.

  • request_time (datetime64, default: None ) –

    Target valid time for the observations. None (default) skips time filtering.

  • time_tolerance ((timedelta64, tuple[timedelta64, timedelta64]), default: None ) –

    Time window used to filter observations around request_time. A single np.timedelta64 creates a symmetric window [-time_tolerance, +time_tolerance]. A 2-tuple (lower, upper) is passed directly to filter_time_range as an asymmetric window. None (default) skips time filtering.

  • return_empty_grid (bool, default: False ) –

    When True, return zero-filled tensors instead of (None, None) when no observations are gridded. Defaults to False.

Returns:

  • y_obs ( Tensor or None ) –

    Gridded observations, shape (1, C, H, W), or None when no observations remain and return_empty_grid is False.

  • mask ( Tensor or None ) –

    Observation count per cell (float), same shape as y_obs, or None under the same condition as above.

docs.title: map_field
docs.text:
Import path: earth2studio.run.map_field

View source on GitHub

docs.title: Documentation
docs.text:
Select the variables and domain of target from x.

Use it to fit fetched data or a model's output to another model's inputs, or to an output subset. batch, time and lead_time are kept from x, as are coordinates that target leaves empty. Exact contiguous selections are views; labels missing from a numeric coordinate select the nearest one. Curvilinear auxiliaries are never indexed as dimensions; model validation checks their geometry at the inference boundary.

map_field selects and never regrids. Nearest selection is accepted only when x covers target: a target label more than one source spacing beyond the source's range (a regional source on a global grid, or a -180..180 longitude source on a 0..360 grid) raises instead of copying edge values. Resolution is not checked, so a source coarser than the target (a 1 degree source on a 0.25 degree grid) repeats neighbouring values. Fetch such data with fetch_data(target_grid=...) or wrap the source in RegriddedSource.

Parameters:

  • x (DataArray) –

    Field to select from

  • target (DataArray | CoordSystem) –

    Signature to select, such as model.input_coords(), or a mapping of coordinate names to labels

Returns:

  • DataArray –

    x on target's coordinates, carrying target's grid metadata when target is a DataArray

Raises:

  • ValueError –

    If a label is missing from a non-numeric coordinate, a numeric coordinate of x does not cover target's range, or the geometry or CRS does not match a DataArray target.

docs.title: README hero image
docs.text:
Regenerate with bash docs/readme_hero/run_all.sh (needs a GPU, network, and EUMETSAT_CONSUMER_KEY / EUMETSAT_CONSUMER_SECRET); output goes to ./hero_out/hero.png.

The wind globe and its legend share Matplotlib's cubehelix palette. Panel headings use 85 px bold type at 88% width, with compact single-line title bands. Both top-row globes use 1500 × 1500 px boxes; the green NVIDIA wordmark uses 60 px type. Heading bands are 152 px tall, with subtitles positioned 116 px below the band's top to leave breathing room beneath the large titles.

docs.title: Scorecards
docs.text:
Warning

The scorecards are in beta. We are actively working on adding more models and improved evaluation.

Forecast skill of Earth2Studio models, one scorecard per model. These show each model's own skill, not a comparison between models. The global models share one campaign: 48 initial conditions (2025), 14-day horizon, ERA5 verification via ARCO_ERA5. Regional models are scored on event campaigns, described on their own pages. Pages are generated from per-model score (JSON) exports, published in the Earth2Studio assets dataset on Hugging Face and produced by the scorecard recipe, which documents how to generate a scorecard for any model; the eval recipe provides the backend support (inference, scoring and metrics).

docs.title: Atlas CRPS
docs.text:
GlobalMRF202680 GBNVIDIAPyTorch

Atlas CRPS is the CRPS-trained ensemble variant of NVIDIA's Atlas weather model. Every forward pass draws a fresh noise vector that modulates each transformer block, so repeated calls from the same initial condition yield calibrated ensemble members. The version scored here runs a 16-member ensemble at 0.25°. It consumes the two most recent analysis frames (t-6 h and t0) and steps forward 6 hours at a time on the native ERA5 721 × 1440 grid.

docs.title: Initialization
docs.text: The Initialization selector in the plot switches between forecasts started from ARCO-ERA5 and from HealDA v2. On the HealDA v2 view the ERA5-initialized run stays as the dashed curve for reference, and both runs are verified against ERA5. HealDA is an AI data assimilation model: a neural network on a HEALPix mesh that turns a window of raw conventional and satellite observations from the NNJA archive directly into a global analysis. A forecast initialized from it runs from observations to prediction. Note : Some inputs like tp06 are not provided by HealDA, so either they can be replaced by ERA5 or a precipitation diagnostic such as PrecipitationAFNOv2.

docs.title: Aurora
docs.text:
GlobalMRF202448 GBMicrosoftPyTorch

Aurora is a foundation model of the atmosphere from Microsoft Research: a 1.3B-parameter Swin-transformer with Perceiver-style encoders pretrained on over a million hours of diverse weather and climate data. The version scored here is the 0.25° deterministic medium-range configuration, which consumes the two most recent analysis frames (t-6h and t0) and steps forward 6 hours at a time on a 720x1440 grid (pole-padded onto ERA5's 721x1440 for verification).

docs.title: Aurora 1.5 Ensemble
docs.text:
GlobalMRF202648 GBMicrosoftPyTorch

Aurora 1.5 Ensemble is the stochastic checkpoint of the Aurora 1.5 atmospheric foundation model from Microsoft. Each forward pass injects fresh Gaussian noise into the backbone conditioning. A batch of identical initial conditions yields independent members. The version scored here runs 16 members at 0.25° on a 720 × 1440 grid. It consumes the two most recent analysis frames, t-6 h and t0. Its state advances every 6 hours while it predicts every hour, so this scorecard carries hourly lead times, verified against hourly ERA5. It covers the outputs ERA5 provides, including dew point, cloud covers, skin temperature, soil temperature, soil moisture, sea ice, and snow depth.

Note : Some inputs like tp06 are not provided by HealDA, so either they can be replaced by ERA5 or a precipitation diagnostic such as PrecipitationAFNOv2.

docs.title: DLWP
docs.text:
GlobalS2S202140 GBNVIDIAPyTorch

Deep Learning Weather Prediction (DLWP) is a compact convolutional model from the University of Washington. It maps the globe onto a cubed sphere and applies a U-Net-style convolutional network on the cube faces, which avoids the polar distortion of a lat/lon grid. The version scored here consumes the two most recent ERA5 analysis frames, 6 hours apart. It forecasts seven variables with a 6-hour step: z at 1000, 700, 500, and 300 hPa, 850 hPa temperature, 2 m temperature, and total column water vapour. The cube faces map back to the 0.25° grid for verification.

docs.title: FCN
docs.text:
GlobalMRF202240 GBNVIDIAPyTorch

FourCastNet (FCN) is NVIDIA's original data-driven global weather model. It uses the Adaptive Fourier Neural Operator, a vision-transformer backbone whose token mixing runs in Fourier space, which made 0.25° global forecasting tractable at the time. The version scored here is the deterministic 26-variable configuration with a 6-hour step, initialized from a single ERA5 analysis frame. It runs on a 720 by 1440 grid that the pipeline maps onto ERA5's 721 by 1440 for verification. Its two relative-humidity levels have no counterpart in the verification store, so the scorecard skips them.

docs.title: FCN3
docs.text:
GlobalMRF202580 GBNVIDIAPyTorch

FourCastNet 3 is NVIDIA's probabilistic machine-learning weather model, built on spherical (geometric) signal processing with a hidden-Markov ensemble formulation: each member evolves its own calibrated stochastic state, so the ensemble spread is learned rather than imposed by initial-condition perturbations. It forecasts 72 atmospheric variables globally at 0.25° resolution with a 6-hour step.

docs.text:
GlobalMRF202340 GBONNX

FengWu is a medium-range forecasting model from Shanghai AI Laboratory. It treats each atmospheric variable as its own modality with a dedicated encoder and decoder and fuses them in a shared transformer. Training uses an uncertainty-weighted multi-task loss and a replay buffer that exposes the model to its own forecasts. The version scored here consumes the two most recent ERA5 analysis frames, 6 hours apart, and forecasts 69 variables at 0.25° resolution with a 6-hour step.

The version scored here consumes the two most recent ERA5 analysis frames, 6 hours apart, and forecasts 70 variables at 0.25° resolution with a 6-hour step. Its 13 relative-humidity levels have no ERA5 counterpart in the verification store and are not scored.

docs.title: Pangu
docs.text:
GlobalMRF202340 GBONNX

Pangu-Weather is Huawei's 3D Earth-specific transformer for medium-range forecasting. It encodes the 13 pressure levels and the surface fields into a single 3D token volume and applies Earth-specific positional biases in its attention blocks. Pangu ships separate networks for 1, 3, 6, and 24-hour steps. The configuration scored here interleaves the 24-hour and 6-hour networks. Each whole day advances with 24-hour steps and the 6-hour network fills the intermediate leads, so daily leads match the 24-hour model exactly. It forecasts 69 variables at 0.25° resolution from a single ERA5 analysis frame.

docs.title: SFNO
docs.text:
GlobalMRF202340 GBNVIDIAPyTorch

SFNO is NVIDIA's Spherical Fourier Neural Operator weather model, the FourCastNet v2 architecture. It replaces the planar Fourier layers of the original FourCastNet with spherical harmonic transforms, so the operator respects the geometry of the globe and stays stable over long forecasts. The version scored here is the deterministic 73-variable configuration at 0.25° resolution with a 6-hour step, initialized from a single ERA5 analysis frame.

docs.title: StormCast
docs.text:
NANWC202440 GBNVIDIAPyTorch

StormCast is NVIDIA's generative convection-allowing model. It forecasts 99 HRRR variables on a 3 km window of the HRRR grid over the central United States with a 1-hour step, conditioned on coarse global fields. A regression network makes a first guess and a diffusion network corrects it, so an ensemble comes from the sampler's noise rather than from perturbed initial conditions.

docs.title: Event-based scoring
docs.text: Unlike the global scorecards, this page comes from an event campaign. Each event is a space-time window over the evaluation data showcasing a physical event. Initial conditions run every 3 hours from 12 hours before the window to its end. The headline curves pool every event's initial conditions, and the Event selector shows one episode at a time. Truth is the HRRR analysis, and scores are uniformly weighted on the model grid. The campaign definition is stormcast_2025_events.yaml and the event scoring lives in the evaluation recipe.

docs.title: Specifications
docs.text: Specs define the required, externally observable behavior of Earth2Studio components. They are contracts for authors, callers, and reviewers, not evidence that an implementation conforms. Code and tests must satisfy the applicable specs.

docs.title: Writing a spec
docs.text:
1. Copy TEMPLATE.md to E2S-<NN>_<TOPIC>_SPEC.md. Assign the next unused number, use the same ID in the title, and add it to the index below. Spec IDs are permanent; do not renumber or reuse them. Cite individual rules as, for example, E2S-06/P1.
  2. Use Purpose and Contract as the top-level sections. Within Contract, group interfaces, requirements, verification, and other details under descriptive subheadings. State the scope and link related contracts.
  3. Describe inputs, outputs, ordering, metadata, ownership, and failure behavior where relevant. Retain public API names only when they define the contract.
  4. Write observable, testable requirements. MUST is required, SHOULD is recommended with a documented reason for exceptions, and MAY is optional.
  5. Give requirements stable IDs, unique within the spec. Preserve existing IDs; never reuse a retired ID for a different requirement.
  6. Add verification criteria covering normal use, boundaries, and failures. Keep them independent of test files and implementation techniques.
  7. Review for ambiguity, conflicting requirements, and broken links. Update the spec when changing a contract; assess compatibility with callers and related specs.

For new requirements, use short, direct sentences. Avoid named-model examples, internal classes, source paths, implementation recipes, rollout history, and speculative features.

Existing specs retain their examples and notes; relocation and formatting do not change their contracts.

docs.title: Index
docs.text:
Initial numbering follows foundational dependencies, then consumers. Integration cross-references may point forward. New specs keep permanent IDs; list prerequisites in their Contract section rather than renumbering existing specs.

ID Spec Contract E2S-01 Core metadata and coordinate systems Coordinate objects, axis names and types, attributes, DataFrame schemas E2S-02 Grids Geometry, identity, coordinates, selection E2S-03 Time statistics Temporal quantities, windows, source aggregation E2S-04 Regridding Mapping fields between grids and composing sources E2S-05 Data fetching Source requests, assembly, members, device placement E2S-06 Models Coordinates, execution, state, hooks, randomness, domains E2S-07 Data assimilation Independent analyses and stateful assimilation E2S-08 Perturbations Transforming ensemble initial conditions E2S-09 Statistics Field reductions and forecast metrics E2S-10 IO Storage templates, writes, metadata, lifecycle E2S-11 Execution Work items, streams, ensembles, distribution, resume E2S-12 Coupling Field exchange and scheduling between components E2S-13 STAC Catalog discovery and raster access

docs.title: E2S-01: Earth2Studio Core Metadata and Coordinate Systems
Purpose
docs.text: Define the metadata that gives field values and tabular records their meaning. Coordinate systems and frame schemas let components declare, compare, and plan inputs and outputs without allocating or reading the data itself.

docs.title: Contract
docs.text: This contract covers coordinate objects, axis names and types, shared attributes, and tabular schemas. Grids owns spatial geometry, CRS, topology, and grid identity. Time statistics owns temporal quantity modifiers, aggregation windows, and their derived metadata. Models defines model-specific coordinate matching and execution; Data fetching defines source requests.

docs.title: Coordinate object
docs.text:
CoordinateSystem is a metadata-only coordinate signature with no field data. It is constructed by coord_array() as an xarray.DataArray whose backing array is a shape-and-dtype-only placeholder. The placeholder stores no field values, reports zero field-data bytes, and rejects conversion to a NumPy array. Indexing and transposing it update the declared shape without allocating field values.

Coordinate labels themselves are real arrays and do occupy memory. An execution DataArray carries actual field values with the same metadata structure. The legacy CoordSystem ordered mapping of axis names to NumPy arrays cannot express the full signature and is not an equivalent object.

ID Requirement C1 A coordinate signature MUST expose ordered dimensions through .dims, lengths through .sizes, labels through .coords, the declared field dtype through .dtype, and shared metadata through .attrs. Planning MUST NOT read or materialize field values; signature .values is unsupported. C2 Dimension names MUST be unique. Dimension order MUST describe field axis order; consumers MUST NOT silently sort, rename, align, or transpose axes when checking a signature. C3 A dimension coordinate MUST be one-dimensional on its namesake dimension and match its size. Auxiliary coordinates MAY be scalar or span multiple declared dimensions; their shape MUST agree with those dimensions. An unlabelled dimension MUST still have a declared size. C4 Dynamic dimensions MUST be explicitly listed in earth2studio_dynamic_dims, form a leading prefix in dimension order, and have size zero in the signature. A fixed zero-sized dimension MUST NOT be interpreted as a wildcard. C5 Resolving dynamic dimensions MUST leave any remaining dynamic dimensions as a leading prefix. Concrete execution inputs MUST satisfy the consuming component's size and nonempty requirements. C6 Metadata operations MUST preserve unaffected coordinate values, order, attributes, name, and field dtype. Replacing an axis MUST remove or recompute dependent auxiliary coordinates and derived metadata so they cannot describe the old labels.

docs.title: Axis names and data types
docs.text:
Known names have the meanings below wherever they occur. These are coordinate types, independent of the field dtype. coord_array() defaults the field dtype to float32; this does not require every field or coordinate to be float32.

Name Coordinate dtype Meaning time NumPy datetime64 Absolute time; initialization/reference time when paired with forecast leads, otherwise valid time. UTC semantics without a timezone-bearing object dtype lead_time NumPy timedelta64 Offset from reference time; may include input history. Negative offsets are permitted where the consuming contract allows history valid_time NumPy datetime64 Auxiliary absolute validity time; when derived from a forecast, equals time + lead_time with the corresponding coordinate dimensions variable String labels Physical quantity identifier from the Earth2Studio vocabulary or a documented extension; temporal qualifiers follow the time-statistics contract ensemble Consistent declared dtype, commonly integers or strings Member identity; labels identify members rather than their array positions batch Declared label dtype, when labelled Generic collection of independent samples. May be unlabelled; when labelled, retain the declared label dtype and order lat, lon Floating-point Geographic coordinates in degrees, as axes or auxiliaries; dimensionality, ordering, and longitude convention follow the grid contract y, x Numeric coordinates or integer indexes Native spatial axes in the grid's native units, or integer indexes for indexed layouts hpx, face, height, width Integer indexes HEALPix pixel or layout indexes; representation and ordering follow the grid contract ID Requirement A1 Known axis names MUST retain the meanings and dtype families above. Custom axes MAY be added with documented meaning, dtype, and ordering. Renamed spatial axes MUST remain identifiable through grid metadata. A2 Concrete temporal labels used for temporal validation MUST be explicit, nonempty, and free of NaT. Numeric offsets MUST NOT substitute for timedelta64. Precision conversion MUST preserve values and avoid overflow; nanosecond precision is not mandatory for all coordinate arrays. A3 variable MUST be a one-dimensional coordinate with unique, nonempty string labels. Labels MUST identify the quantity and its units consistently across producers and consumers. A4 Coordinate order MUST be preserved. Uniqueness or monotonicity beyond variable is imposed by the consuming contract, not assumed globally; repeated requested times, for example, may repeat labels. A5 A source's member argument selects the ensemble axis; it MUST NOT introduce a second standard axis named member.

docs.title: Standard attributes
docs.text:
Signature attributes live on the DataArray; descriptive attributes may also live on individual coordinates. A name or descriptive attribute does not replace coordinate labels or establish axis order.

Attribute Location Type and role earth2studio_kind Signature String "coordinate_array"; identifies a coordinate signature earth2studio_schema_version Signature Integer 1; version of the signature metadata format earth2studio_dynamic_dims Signature Ordered tuple of dimension names; empty when all dimensions are fixed units Coordinate or homogeneous field String describing the units of its values source Field or DataFrame Producer/provenance identifier string; distinct from a DataFrame's per-row source column ID Requirement M1 Signature construction MUST set kind, schema version, and dynamic dimensions consistently with the object. Concrete field outputs MUST omit these three signature-only attributes. M2 Descriptive attributes are optional. When present, they MUST describe the associated values accurately. A single field-level units MUST NOT claim one meaning for a mixed-variable field; variable-dependent descriptions belong on coordinates indexed by variable. M3 Metadata-preserving transformations MUST retain unrelated user attributes and coordinate attributes. Attributes invalidated by a transformation MUST be updated or removed. M4 Grid identity/CRS attributes and earth2studio_statistics MUST obey their owning specs. They MUST NOT be independently inferred from field shape or copied onto incompatible coordinates.

docs.title: DataFrame schema objects
docs.text:
A DataFrame represents rows of observations, forecasts, or analyses rather than a dense Cartesian product of axes. Column names carry meaning; its row index is not a replacement for time, location, or variable columns. CPU frames use pandas; GPU-capable interfaces may use cuDF with the same logical schema.

Two declarations serve different roles:

  • FrameSchema is an ordered mapping from column names to one-dimensional NumPy arrays. An empty array declares a column's dtype with dynamic values; a nonempty array declares acceptable values, such as supported variable labels. The arrays are column constraints, not equal-length sample rows.
  • PyArrow Schema describes source fields by name, type, nullability, and optional field metadata. A source exposes its schema as SCHEMA. E2STUDIO_SCHEMA supplies the shared field vocabulary and suggested types.
ID Requirement F1 Schema column names MUST be unique. A FrameSchema MUST declare required columns and their dtype/value constraints; a consumer MUST validate those requirements before using the rows. An empty constraint array MUST NOT require an empty DataFrame. F2 A source schema MUST declare each supported field's type and nullability. Standard field names MUST retain the meanings below; sources SHOULD use the suggested types, documenting deviations. Additional source-specific fields MAY be declared. F3 Field selection MUST preserve requested column order. fields=None selects the full source schema; a name or list selects those fields; a PyArrow schema selects fields with matching source types. Unknown fields MUST raise KeyError; incompatible requested Arrow types MUST raise TypeError. F4 Returned columns MUST satisfy the selected source schema, including on an empty result. Null values are permitted only for nullable fields. A projected subset need not contain all core columns, but MUST be checked against a consuming FrameSchema before execution. F5 Field metadata MAY include description, units, and source_name; source_name describes the upstream name and MUST NOT replace the public column name. Source frames MUST identify the producer in frame.attrs["source"]. F6 Forecast frame schemas MUST declare lead_time as a duration when exposing forecast offsets, with time interpreted as reference time. If valid_time is exposed, it MUST equal time + lead_time.

docs.title: Standard DataFrame fields
docs.text:
These tables define a vocabulary, not a requirement that every frame contain every column. The source schema and consuming FrameSchema determine presence. The shared Arrow schema permits nulls in all listed fields; a source or consumer may impose stricter constraints. Physical units of observation follow variable.

Name Suggested Arrow type Meaning time timestamp[ns] Observation time, or forecast reference time; UTC lat float32 Latitude in degrees, within [-90, 90] lon float32 Longitude in degrees, within [0, 360] elev float32 Observation elevation above the surface, metres observation float32 Measurement or predicted value of the identified variable variable string Earth2Studio quantity identifier pres float32 Observation pressure level, Pa type, class string Observation type identifier and class source, station string Per-row source and station identifiers station_elev float32 Station elevation, metres quality uint16 Quality-control marker; 0 is best, 15 is missing satellite string Satellite platform identifier scan_angle float32 Satellite scan angle, degrees sensor_index uint16 Sensor channel index solza, solaza float32 Solar zenith and azimuth angles, degrees satellite_za, satellite_aza float32 Satellite zenith and azimuth angles, degrees wavenumber float64 Channel wavenumber, cm^-1 track_id, storm_name, basin string Track identifier, storm name, and basin code season int32 Tropical cyclone season year

Forecast extensions to this shared vocabulary are:

Name Suggested Arrow type Meaning lead_time duration[ns] Forecast offset from time valid_time timestamp[ns] Optional absolute forecast validity time

docs.title: Verification
docs.text:
• Inspect a signature's dimensions, sizes, labels, dtype, and attributes without accessing field values (C1); reject duplicate dimensions or mismatched sizes (C2–C3).
  • Resolve a dynamic prefix and check that fixed empty axes remain fixed and a non-leading wildcard is rejected (C4–C5).
  • Check temporal dtype families, NaT, variable uniqueness, and preservation of label order, including repeated times (A1–A4).
  • Replace a variable or lead-time axis and verify dependent metadata is removed or recomputed while unrelated metadata survives (C6, M2–M4).
  • Convert a signature to a concrete field and check signature-only attrs are absent (M1).
  • Validate a frame against dynamic and value-constrained columns; select source fields in a different order and exercise unknown names, incompatible types, nullability, and empty results (F1–F4).
  • Check source provenance and forecast validity-time consistency (F5–F6).

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text: Provide one lightweight contract for describing spatial grids without coupling grid geometry to field data or regridding engines. This protocol describes grids only; it does not select interpolation methods, construct weights, or transform field data.

docs.title: Interface
docs.text:
GridDefinition is a runtime-checkable structural protocol. Implementations satisfy the interface directly; inheritance is not required.

@runtime_checkable
class GridDefinition(Protocol):
    @property
    def dims(self) -> tuple[str, ...]: ...

    @property
    def shape(self) -> tuple[int, ...]: ...

    @property
    def topology(self) -> GridTopology: ...

    @property
    def crs(self) -> pyproj.CRS | None: ...

    def coords(self, indexes=None, *, only_index=False) -> xr.Coordinates: ...
    def subset_indexers(
        self,
        coordinates,
        *,
        bounds=None,
        bounds_crs=None,
    ) -> dict[str, object]: ...
    def cell_bounds(self, indexes) -> xr.Coordinates | None: ...
    @property
    def attrs(self) -> dict[str, object]: ...
    def fingerprint(self) -> str: ...
  • dims defines authoritative spatial dimension order
  • shape sizes each dimension in the same order
  • topology identifies the geometry family
  • crs describes native coordinates when PyProj can represent them
  • coords() returns complete Xarray coordinates, or dimension indexes with only_index=True
  • subset_indexers() translates supported selections into Xarray indexers
  • cell_bounds() returns optional geographic cell geometry
  • attrs returns a JSON-serializable description for Xarray and agents
  • fingerprint() returns stable geometry identity for validation and caching

docs.title: Package
docs.text:
Grid definitions live in earth2studio.grids, with one implementation per file. The package initializer exports definitions and owns the process-local registry.

Definition Dimensions Topology Native CRS LatLonGrid lat, lon Rectilinear Geographic ProjectedGrid y, x Projected Required CurvilinearGrid y, x Curvilinear None PointGrid x Points None HEALPixGrid hpx or face, height, width HEALPix None

Users may implement the protocol directly for other grid families.

docs.title: Populating Xarray Coordinates
docs.text:
A definition provides complete coordinates in one call:

array = xr.DataArray(data, dims=definition.dims, coords=definition.coords())

Dimension coordinates preserve definition.dims. Projected, curvilinear, point, and HEALPix definitions add latitude and longitude as auxiliary coordinates. Use only_index=True when only inexpensive dimension indexes are needed:

indexes = definition.coords(only_index=True)

Selected index values avoid generating geographic coordinates for the full grid:

coordinates = definition.coords({"y": selected_y, "x": selected_x})

docs.title: Allocation-free model signatures
docs.text:
earth2studio.utils.coord_array consumes the same definitions without allocating field values. It supplies grid sizes, index coordinates, serializable grid attrs, and earth2studio_crs from definition.crs. Curvilinear and point grids also supply geographic coordinates. A registered string adds earth2studio_grid_id.

signature = coord_array(
    ("batch", "variable", "lat", "lon"),
    {"variable": ["t2m"]},
    dynamic=("batch",),
    grid="latlon-0.25deg-south-pole-excluded",
)

Models using projected grids use the standard y, x dimensions, preserving native coordinate values in the CRS's units. The grid supplies these axes and geographic coordinates; infer_grid() can recover the geometry without renaming.

Optional grid_dims maps standard grid axes to a model's dimension names, including grid-coordinate dimensions and the dims metadata. Explicit coordinates use the mapped names. This mapping does not rename the grid definition itself: rename model axes back before passing such an array to infer_grid() or grid selection methods.

A crop has different axes and shape from its full parent grid. Construct a new definition with the selected native axes and the same CRS, then pass that definition to coord_array. For example, for a projected parent grid:

crop = ProjectedGrid(parent.y[10:20], parent.x[30:50], parent.crs)
signature = coord_array(("y", "x"), grid=crop)

This produces the cropped axes and their geographic coordinates without attaching the full parent's registered ID. Using grid="hrrr", for example, requests the entire registered HRRR geometry, not a crop; attaching that ID to cropped data would incorrectly claim that its geometry matches the full registered grid.

Coordinate handshakes compare fixed axes and auxiliary coordinates and require matching declared grid ID and CRS metadata. coord_array_like() creates output signatures from validated inputs without recreating or reprojecting their grid.

docs.title: Model coordinates to target grid
docs.text:
The grid contract must support the round trip GridDefinition -> coord_array -> infer_grid -> GridDefinition. Coordinate arrays store spatial coordinates and serializable grid metadata, not live grid objects. Non-spatial model dimensions, including empty dynamic dimensions, must not affect reconstruction.

The reconstructed target grid owns its geometry, extent, and CRS at construction. Consumers such as fetch_data can obtain spatial requirements from that object without asking callers for separate bounds or CRS arguments. Extent computation belongs to the grid implementation and must respect topology and longitude wrap; a bounding rectangle alone is not a complete grid description.

Reconstruction must preserve actual coordinate values, crops, axis order, and CRS. A registered grid ID must not cause changed coordinates to be replaced by the parent geometry merely because their shapes match. Renamed model axes must be recoverable from coordinate metadata without caller-side renaming.

Standard-layout reconstruction exists today. Metadata-driven reconstruction of renamed axes, validation of registered geometry against coordinate values, and an explicit grid-owned extent interface are required follow-up work. The manual renaming guidance above describes the current implementation until that support lands. Fetch-side regridding onto a target grid is specified in E2S-05_FETCH_DATA_SPEC.md.

Until that validation lands, a registered earth2studio_grid_id is trusted: infer_grid() and handshake_dataarray() compare only dimension names and sizes for labelled data. Data whose latitude was reversed, whose longitude was rolled or converted to -180..180, or which was otherwise reordered after it was labelled is still accepted as the registered grid and read in the wrong order. Drop the label (array.attrs.pop("earth2studio_grid_id")) after reordering spatial axes so the actual coordinates are used.

docs.title: HEALPix Representations
docs.text:
HEALPix ordering and storage layout are explicit. nested and ring use a flat hpx dimension. xy supports flat hpx storage or an expanded (face, height, width) layout. XY also records its face origin and winding so layouts such as Earth2Grid's HEALPIX_PAD_XY are unambiguous:

dlesym = grids.HEALPixGrid(
    level=6,
    ordering="xy",
    layout="face",
    xy_origin="north",
    xy_clockwise=True,
)

docs.title: Registry
docs.text:
The process-local registry maps stable names and aliases to complete definitions:

grids.register_grid("regional-lcc", definition, aliases=("regional",))
definition = grids.resolve_grid("regional")
names = grids.list_grids()

Registration validates protocol conformance, dimensions, shape, index coordinates, serializable metadata, and a nonempty fingerprint. Re-registering an identical definition is a no-op; conflicting names and aliases raise an error. Names recognized as CRS input by PyProj are reserved.

docs.title: Inferring Grid Type
docs.text:
infer_grid() follows an explicit-to-general chain:

  1. Resolve and validate earth2studio_grid_id
  2. Infer a projected grid from y, x, and earth2studio_crs
  3. Infer rectilinear, point, or curvilinear layouts from latitude and longitude
  4. Raise when no supported layout is unambiguous

PointGrid is the fallback for arbitrary samples represented as lat(x) and lon(x). Generic lat(hpx) and lon(hpx) are not enough to distinguish HEALPix ordering, layout, or level, so HEALPix requires a registered grid identifier.

docs.title: Selection
docs.text:
Selection returns positional Xarray indexers and never receives field data. Every definition supports geographic bounds and optional bounds_crs. HEALPix also supports face selection when its ordering identifies faces.

indexers = definition.subset_indexers(
    coordinates,
    bounds=(-125, 25, -65, 50),
    bounds_crs="EPSG:4326",
)
subset = array.isel(indexers)

Bounds (min_x, min_y, max_x, max_y) are inclusive limits on cell centres. In a geographic bounds_crs (the default), longitude bounds are independent of the grid's longitude convention: a cell is selected when its longitude lies at most max_x - min_x degrees east of min_x, modulo 360. So (0, 180) includes the 180° meridian on both 0..360 and -180..180 grids; (-190, -170), (170, 190) and (170, -170) select the same 20° box across the dateline; and min_x > max_x wraps eastward through the dateline, as Region.box does. Unlike Region.box, which rejects a 360° span in favour of Region.band, a span of 360° or more selects every longitude. Projected bounds are compared without wrapping.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text: Declare temporal quantities in variable labels, and have data sources produce them. Native data sources own temporal aggregation; fetch_data forwards supported labels and preserves their metadata. Sampling and reduction belong to the source.

docs.title: Declarations and Ownership
docs.text:
Qualified variable labels identify temporal quantities unambiguously:

variables = ["u10m", "t2m:mean:1day", "t2m:mean:1week", "t2m:max:30days"]

The first : separates the source name from its modifier; base names cannot contain :. Raw backend identifiers containing :: are passed through unchanged, not parsed as statistic labels. Unqualified labels retain their source-defined meaning (including native accumulation periods). Qualified labels are canonical for model and output coordinates. Coordinate constructors derive statistics metadata from these labels; there is no separate statistics= declaration.

Data sources own aggregation: they accept qualified labels for the quantities they support and return them reduced (see Source Responsibilities). time_statistics owns modifier normalization, window planning, metadata, and block reductions. earth2studio.data.utils provides shared request planning and window reduction.

docs.title: Windows
docs.text:
For valid time T, intervals are half-open and right-closed: a window ending at T includes the sample stamped T and excludes the one stamped at its start.

Modifier Selected interval mean:24h (T - 24h, T] mean:-12h:+12h (T - 12h, T + 12h]

At source cadence Δ, a window (T + start, T + end] reads the stamps T + start + Δ, …, T + end. The earth2studio_statistics metadata records this as closed: "right".

Built-in methods are mean, sum, min, and max, which propagate missing samples (see Planning and Reduction). Source cadence must divide the window exactly. Durations are integers with units ns, us, ms, s/sec/second, m/min/minute, h/hr/hour, d/day, or w/wk/week; plural names are accepted. Weeks are seven days. Month and year durations are unsupported: specify an explicit number of days or hours instead (for example, 30days). M and Y are rejected rather than interpreted as minutes or fixed calendar approximations; use lowercase m for minutes. NumPy month/year timedeltas are also rejected as source cadences.

docs.title: Accumulations and Means of Instantaneous Fields
docs.text:
Accumulations and mean rates are stamped at the end of their period: hourly ARCO-ERA5 tp, ttr, ro and sf and HRRR forecast tp hold (t - 1h, t] at stamp t, and so do 6-hourly model outputs such as tp06. Right-closed windows match this, so a two-part label covers the period ending at T at any cadence:

Label at T Hourly stamps read Physical period tp:sum:6h T-5h … T (T - 6h, T] tp06 (ARCO alias) T-5h … T (T - 6h, T]

On 6-hourly tp06 frames, tp:sum:24h reads T-18h … T, the 24 hours ending at T. For instantaneous fields a window holds the samples after its start up to and including its end, so t2m:max:24h at T reads T-23h … T hourly. Use explicit offsets when a different set of samples is wanted, as ORBIT-2 does for its daily extremes (t2m:max:-25h:-1h reads T-24h … T-1h).

Running buckets that reset periodically (GFS tp) cannot be summed: the buckets overlap, so tp:sum:Nh double counts; use tp06. Each affected source states this in its Temporal statistics: note.

docs.title: Calendar-Day Means: FuXi-S2S
docs.text:
FuXi-S2S labels days by starting midnight, consumes two consecutive daily means, and predicts the next. All 76 channels declare means with these hourly windows:

Quantity Qualified label Samples relative to day start Ordinary fields t2m:mean:-1h:23h 00–23 UTC Hourly precipitation accumulations tp:mean:0h:24h 01 UTC through next 00 UTC Hourly thermal radiation accumulations ttr:mean:0h:24h 01 UTC through next 00 UTC

tp and ttr cover the day itself, (T, T + 24h], because their timestamps mark interval ends: 24 hourly samples from 01 UTC through next-day 00 UTC. Ordinary fields take the instantaneous samples 00–23 UTC, (T - 1h, T + 23h]. These means retain one-hour accumulation units; multiply predicted tp by 24 for a daily total. Channel order and model-unit conversions are unchanged.

Preserve start-of-day timestamps and one-day lead increments. Substituting mean:24h would select the preceding day. The source must sample hourly; a source storing these daily means returns them under the same labels without reducing again.

docs.title: Source Responsibilities
docs.text:
A source that supports a temporal quantity accepts its qualified label in variable, like any other variable, and:

  • returns it under the requested spelling, with its entry recorded in earth2studio_statistics (see Metadata and Scope);
  • anchors windows to valid time for analysis sources, and to each lead time within one initialization for forecast sources, never reducing across initializations;
  • reduces on its native grid before returning, so wrappers and fetch_data regrid one reduced field rather than every sample;
  • raises, before fetching, for a modifier it does not support, for duplicate normalized quantities such as t2m:mean:24h and t2m:mean:1day, and for a window its cadence cannot sample exactly or whose required coordinates fall outside the source's availability;
  • documents when base fields are already accumulations: reducing stored values does not automatically deaccumulate them or integrate a rate over time.

How a quantity is produced is the source's choice. It may read a stored aggregate, compose native accumulations as ARCO_ERA5 does for tp, or fetch instantaneous samples at its cadence and reduce them. Sampling cadence is internal to the source; no public time_step property is required.

Document native support in the source class docstring in a Note headed Temporal statistics:: methods, label syntax, cadence, window closure, and accumulation caveats. Capability metadata belongs on the source's lexicon as TIME_STATISTICS, a tuple of supported method names. Sources expose their lexicon through lexicon; they do not expose time_statistics or time_step attributes. An absent lexicon declaration means no native support. fetch_data discovers support through the lexicon (and through wrapped/component sources) and rejects unsupported methods before fetching.

docs.title: Planning and Reduction
docs.text:
Sources that reduce instantaneous samples use the shared primitives:

time_step = np.timedelta64(6, "h")
times = source_times("mean:24h", valid_time, time_step)
leads = source_lead_times("mean:24h", lead_time, time_step)
result = apply_time_statistic(block, "mean:24h", valid_time, time_step)

Planning accepts scalar or array targets. Forecast sources retain initialization time and plan lead times. Planners can produce negative leads; a source must reject unavailable leads before downloading, rather than switch to an earlier forecast.

apply_time_statistic reduces a variable block for one scalar target, excluding values outside the window and rejecting missing or duplicate required coordinates. It selects lead_time when present, otherwise time; callers may override the dimension. Xarray preserves NumPy, CuPy, or Dask execution without implicit transfers.

docs.title: Native source request pipeline
docs.text:
Two functions in earth2studio.data.utils support the source's own request model:

  1. plain, stats, attrs = plan_statistics(variable, target_times, delta_t, supported, validate=...) splits the requested labels and plans the samples. supported is the lexicon's TIME_STATISTICS. target_times are the output valid times (or the lead times of one initialization for forecast sources) and delta_t the source cadence. plain is [(slot, name)] of unqualified labels (including raw :: identifiers), which the source fetches with its ordinary path. stats is a list of StatisticPlan dataclasses with slot, base, modifier, and samples fields. samples contains the coordinates to read, shaped (target, sample) (source_times / source_lead_times). Malformed labels, unsupported methods, empty base names and duplicate normalized quantities raise ValueError. attrs is the output's earth2studio_statistics metadata.
  2. validate is called once with the sorted unique sample coordinates (datetime, or timedelta for lead time targets) before anything is read, so the source rejects unavailable samples with its own _validate_time / _validate_leadtime.
  3. await reduce_statistics(out, stats, fetch) with out the (target, variable, ...) output view (per initialization for forecasts) and fetch(coord, base) a source coroutine returning one field with the lexicon conversion applied. For each target and statistic variable, the fields are fetched concurrently into a transient array (sample, ...), reduced through the registered statistic (reduce_samples, an xarray reduction over the sample dimension) and written to out. The stack is then released. Finally the source sets array.attrs.update(attrs).
flowchart TD
    A["source.fetch"] --> B["plan_statistics"]
    B --> C["plain variables → source's ordinary request path"]
    B --> D["statistics: samples per target"]
    D --> E["source._validate_time / _validate_leadtime"]
    E --> F["reduce_statistics → source fetch(coord, base)"]
    F --> G["transient stack → reduce_samples (registered statistic)"]
    G --> H["out[target, slot]"]
    C --> H
    H --> I["array.attrs.update(attrs)"]

ARCO and WB2 read fields through fetch_array; GFS and HRRR through an async _fetch_sample that resolves the index record (GFS also rebuilds tp06 from accumulation buckets) and calls fetch_array. Plain variables keep each source's existing request path (for example ARCO's shared chunk reads).

Memory is bounded by the output plus at most four transient stacks of one window each and async_workers (default 4) in-flight fields; a stack is released as soon as it is reduced. Coordinate plans grow with the number of requested samples. Overlapping windows of different targets re-read their common samples; this trades repeated reads (usually served by the source's disk cache) for the simplicity of an independent reduction per target. The jobs run through a fixed worker pool and a task group: a failure, timeout or caller cancellation cancels and awaits outstanding fetches, and no partial window is ever written.

Missing samples propagate: if any sample in a window is NaN, mean, sum, min and max return NaN for that cell, so a field built from a missing value is never silently partial. This covers cells masked by the source (such as SST over land) and records a source could not resolve (for example a GRIB record absent from its index, which sources return as an all-NaN field with a warning). Skipping missing samples is a data-handling choice, not part of a quantity's label, so it is not expressed as a statistic method. The reduction does not use a cadence, window or expected count; the source plans the coordinates. Means are sample-weighted, not duration-weighted. Sources propagate fetching failures rather than reduce a partial window.

docs.title: Implemented source capabilities
docs.text:
All sources below declare ("mean", "sum", "min", "max") on their lexicon.

Source Sampling Window axis ARCO_ERA5 1 hour Valid time WB2ERA5, WB2ERA5_121x240, WB2ERA5_32x64 6 hours Valid time GFS 6 hours Valid time GFS_FX 1 hour Lead within initialization HRRR 1 hour Valid time HRRR_FX 1 hour Lead within initialization

Source-specific considerations:

  • ARCO derived overlapping accumulation periods can double-count totals.
  • WB2 overlapping tp12 / tp24 samples double-count rainfall.
  • GFS raw tp uses resetting buckets; analysis tp06 uses the preceding cycle's complete six-hour bucket. Forecast tp06 requires leads ≥6h; overlapping totals must not be interpreted as disjoint rainfall.
  • HRRR reductions operate on source-defined stored values.
  • All forecast sources require expanded leads to be available for each initialization.

WB2Climatology does not declare native statistics. Hourly planning does not interpolate missing forecast leads; source availability validation remains binding.

Custom block reductions share the window syntax and must preserve non-time dimensions, including variable:

register_time_statistic("range", lambda x, dim: x.max(dim) - x.min(dim))

Native sources reduce through the registry, so a registered statistic works once the source lists its name in the lexicon's TIME_STATISTICS. Standalone apply_time_statistic also accepts registered statistics.

docs.title: Metadata and Scope
docs.text:
time_statistic_metadata() returns normalized modifier, method, window, offsets, and interval closure. Durations remain np.timedelta64 until serialization. Native results record qualified labels in earth2studio_statistics:

array.attrs["earth2studio_statistics"] = {
    "t2m:mean:1day": time_statistic_metadata("mean:1day")
}

Labels carry quantity identity through handshakes; attributes support lookup and serialization. Record CF-compatible time bounds and cell_methods when supported.

Irregular-cadence inference, cross-variable diagnostics, and fused GPU kernels are out of scope. The native helpers operate on NumPy fields.

docs.title: Verification
docs.text: Keep one mocked statistics test per source (extend its existing call mock when present). Mock backend I/O, retaining real parsing, planning, validation, and aggregation. Cover all four reductions, plain/statistic mixtures, metadata, overlapping-window fetch sharing, request order, NaNs, and invalid windows. Forecast cases also cover distinct initializations and unavailable/negative leads. Shared fixtures live in test/data/conftest.py; block-window tests live in test/utils/test_time_statistics.py.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text:
Provide one contract for mapping a field from one grid onto another, so models can recommend a source on another grid for an input slot and drivers can fetch it without knowing the method. Any regridder, built in or wrapping an external engine, works under the same interface.

Grid geometry follows E2S-02_GRID_SPEC.md; this contract covers only moving field data between two such geometries.

Status: the protocol is in earth2studio/grids/base.py, with NearestRegridder and BilinearRegridder as built-in implementations and a method registry in earth2studio.grids. RegriddedSource, CompositeSource and CompositeForecastSource live in earth2studio.data.

docs.title: Interface
docs.text:
Regridder is a runtime-checkable structural protocol over xr.DataArray.

@runtime_checkable
class Regridder(Protocol):
    @property
    def source_grid(self) -> GridDefinition: ...

    @property
    def target_grid(self) -> GridDefinition: ...

    def __call__(self, x: xr.DataArray) -> xr.DataArray: ...
    def to(self, device) -> Regridder: ...
  • source_grid and target_grid are fixed at construction.
  • __call__ maps the spatial dimensions of one field; other dimensions pass through.
  • to optionally places precomputed state on a device ahead of use.

It is a protocol rather than an ABC because there is no shared implementation to inherit. Wrappers around external engines conform without subclassing.

docs.title: Rules
docs.text:
Rule Requirement R1 Indices and weights are computed at construction; __call__ only applies them R2 __call__ raises ValueError if spatial dims, sizes or labels differ from source_grid R3 Output dims are the non-spatial dims of x, in order, then target_grid.dims R4 Spatial coords and grid metadata match coord_array(..., grid=target_grid) R5 Output keeps the array backing (NumPy or CuPy) and device of x R6 __call__ has no observable side effects, so one instance can be shared R7 Target points without source coverage get a documented fill value, NaN by default R8 A regridder never fetches data
  • R2: dimension coordinate labels, where the field has them, must match the grid's in order, so a field with flipped latitude is rejected rather than silently mis-mapped.
  • R3: non-spatial coordinates and attributes pass through. Grid-owned attributes (earth2studio_grid_id, earth2studio_crs and the CRS attributes) follow target_grid under R4, so the output handshakes against a slot declared on target_grid without further coordinate assembly.
  • R5: a call must accept fields on any supported device, whether or not to was called. Caching device copies of precomputed state is allowed under R6.
  • R7: the fill applies only where the source has no coverage. NaNs in the source data propagate and are never replaced by the fill. How a regridder is told its fill is up to its constructor; it is not part of the protocol. The built-ins take fill_value, where None means no fill is allowed and construction raises ValueError if any target point lacks coverage.
  • Floating dtypes are preserved. Other dtypes may be promoted so the fill is representable.
  • NearestRegridder takes an optional source_mask shaped like the source grid; masked points are never selected, so a land-masked ocean field fills every target from its nearest valid point. The mask is fixed at construction (R1), unlike NaNs in the data, which propagate (R7).

docs.title: Registry
docs.text:
Regridders register under a method name with register_regridder(method, cls). A registered class declares the grid pairs it handles with a supports(source_grid, target_grid) class method and is constructed as cls(source_grid, target_grid, **options).

  • list_regridders(source, target) lists the methods available for a pair.
  • resolve_regridder(source, target, method="nearest", **options) constructs the most recently registered supporting class. This lets grid-specific implementations, registered after the built-ins, take precedence. It raises ValueError when no class supports the pair. fetch_data takes regridder objects, not method names; callers resolve a method themselves.
  • The built-ins register as "nearest", for any grid with geographic coordinates, and "bilinear", for structured sources.
  • A class registered as "nearest" must accept max_dist_km="auto" and fill_value=None, which fetch_data passes when it regrids automatically.

General regridders support grid families rather than enumerated grids, because model grids are usually crops that are never registered.

docs.title: Composition
docs.text:
RegriddedSource(source, regridder) pairs a data or forecast source with a regridder bound to its grid. It is an ordinary source: calling it fetches from the wrapped source and regrids each returned field. A model recommending a source off its slot's grid returns the pair from default_sources(), and drivers fetch from it like any other source:

def default_sources(self):
    return (MRMS(), RegriddedSource(GOES(), NearestRegridder(goes_grid, self.grid)))

The pair preserves lexicon-based statistics discovery and forwards device, and declares is_forecast. It passes qualified variable labels to the source, which aggregates on its native grid, and regrids the reduced field. A regridder is bound to its source's grid, so a caller replacing the source must replace the whole pair (R2 raises otherwise).

CompositeSource(sources, variables) and CompositeForecastSource(sources, variables) route each requested variable to the one named component that provides it, matching qualified labels by base name, and join the parts along variable:

  • CompositeSource is an analysis source, (time, variable), and rejects forecast components.
  • CompositeForecastSource is a forecast source, (time, lead_time, variable). It passes requests to forecast components unchanged, and fetches analysis components at the valid times time + lead_time, labelled by the requested times and leads.
  • Components must return fields on one device.
  • They must share every coordinate other than variable. A component on another grid is wrapped in a RegriddedSource onto the shared target.

docs.title: Migration
docs.text:
The eval recipe's tensor-native Regridder ABC (recipes/eval/src/regrid.py) and its NearestNeighborRegridder and BilinearRegridder map onto the built-ins. Its RegriddedSource and CompositeSource map onto the core compositions. Two differences matter when migrating:

  • The built-ins take grid definitions rather than coordinate arrays.
  • The built-ins fill with NaN by default. Pass fill_value=0 where the recipe relied on its bilinear default.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text:
earth2studio.data.fetch_data adapts analysis and forecast sources to a field xr.DataArray with consistent time, lead-time, and variable dimensions. It owns source dispatch, output assembly, device placement, and the order in which regridding is applied. Native data sources own temporal aggregation; fetch_data forwards supported labels and preserves their metadata.

This contract reflects the API in PR #1170. Temporal windows follow E2S-03_TIME_STATISTICS_SPEC.md; spatial geometry follows E2S-02_GRID_SPEC.md and regridding follows E2S-04_REGRID_SPEC.md.

docs.title: Interface
docs.text:
def fetch_data(
    source: DataSource | ForecastSource,
    time: TimeArray,
    variable: VariableArray,
    lead_time: LeadTimeArray = np.array([np.timedelta64(0, "h")]),
    device: torch.device | str = "cpu",
    target_grid: GridDefinition | None = None,
    regridder: Regridder | None = None,
    member: int | str | Sequence | MemberArray | None = None,
) -> xr.DataArray:
    ...
  • time contains initialization timestamps; lead_time contains offsets from each timestamp. Both must be nonempty one-dimensional NumPy arrays of datetime and timedelta values respectively, without NaT.
  • variable is a nonempty one-dimensional array of requested labels, optionally qualified with a temporal statistic.
  • device accepts CPU or CUDA destinations. CUDA output requires CuPy.
  • target_grid is the grid to return fields on, typically infer_grid(model.input_coords()); use resolve_grid for a registered name. Without it, fields stay on the source grid.
  • regridder is a Regridder to apply (see E2S-04_REGRID_SPEC.md). Choosing a method, or a registered one with resolve_regridder, is the caller's job.
  • member names one member or distinct members to fetch from an ensemble source, in the source's own labels (see Ensemble Members). Other sources reject it with ValueError.

There is no separate metadata or statistics input. Temporal quantities are declared in variable labels. target_grid replaces the former interp_to, and regridder replaces interp_method. Sampling cadence belongs to the source.

docs.title: Regridding
docs.text:
fetch_data maps the field the source returns; it never inspects how the source produced it, so a RegriddedSource is fetched like any other source.

Arguments Behavior Neither Fields stay on the source grid regridder Applied; with target_grid, it must produce that grid target_grid only Inferred source grid mapped onto it, cautiously, as below

Mapping onto target_grid infers the source grid from the fetched field with infer_grid and raises ValueError if it cannot. Then:

  1. Fields already on the target pass through.
  2. A target that is an exact crop of the source, on rectilinear or projected grids with the same CRS, is selected by label without interpolation.
  3. Otherwise a nearest-neighbor regridder is resolved with max_dist_km="auto" and fill_value=None, and applied with an info log. The regridder raises ValueError if any target point lies beyond the source's resolution, and fetch_data re-raises it rather than fill; a caller wanting fills passes a Regridder configured for them.

Step 3 constructs a regridder on every call. Callers fetching repeatedly on one pair of grids, or wanting another method, should build a Regridder once and pass it. The helpers behind steps 1 and 2, same_geometry and select_subset, are public in earth2studio.grids.

docs.title: Order of Operations
docs.text:
1. Fetch requested fields, including source-computed temporal statistics.
  2. Assemble requested labels and their statistics metadata on the source grid. Cast floating fields to float32; other dtypes pass through.
  3. Move the result to device if it is not already there.
  4. Map onto the target grid on device.

Models consume float32, and sources may build float64 arrays (for example with a bare np.empty), so fetch_data owns the cast. A DataArray from a source called directly keeps the source's dtype.

Regridding requested through fetch_data follows reduction. A RegriddedSource regrids whatever its wrapped source returns, after any temporal reduction.

docs.title: Source Backing and Device
docs.text: Data sources accept a device keyword, default "cpu", and expose it as a device attribute holding a torch.device. On a CUDA device, field sources return CuPy-backed DataArrays and dataframe sources return cuDF frames. The source protocol is unchanged, and a source without the attribute is a CPU source. RegriddedSource and the composites forward the attribute; composites compare devices with the CUDA index made explicit, so cuda matches the current device. fetch_data accepts either backing and moves data only in step 3. Reduction backing is implementation specific: the native helpers currently reduce NumPy fields before source device conversion.

docs.title: Source Dispatch
docs.text:
A source whose __call__ signature contains lead_time is a forecast source. Wrappers that forward requests through *args, such as RegriddedSource, declare this instead with a boolean is_forecast property. CompositeSource and CompositeForecastSource have explicit signatures:

Source Call Temporal interpretation DataSource source(valid_time, variable) Absolute valid timestamps ForecastSource source(time, lead_time, variable) Leads within each initialization

For instantaneous analysis requests, fetch at time + lead_time for each lead, then restore the requested initialization timestamps and add a lead_time dimension. For instantaneous forecasts, request initialization times and leads directly. Select returned coordinates in request order.

Sources must label their output with the requested time (and, for forecast sources, lead_time) values, in request order; repeated requests may repeat a label. A source that maps a request onto other stored timestamps (a daily product truncating sub-day times, nearest-time matching) still returns the requested labels, and may record the timestamps it actually read in an auxiliary coordinate (CMIP6 uses time_selected). fetch_data selects by label and never relabels positionally: a source returning other labels raises a ValueError naming the source and the labels it did not return, rather than silently attaching data to the wrong time.

docs.title: Ensemble Members
docs.text:
Ensemble forecasts and stored ensemble runs supply one field per member, and an ensemble run may start each member from a different one: for example four seeded branches from each of 50 IFS ENS members, member m starting from forecast member m // 4 + 1. Members are therefore a request coordinate, like lead_time, on the sources that have them:

IFS_ENS()(time, variable)                     # unchanged: the configured member
IFS_ENS()(time, variable, member=[3, 4])      # leading ensemble dimension: 3, 4
IFS_ENS()(time, variable, member=3)           # leading ensemble dimension: 3
fetch_data(IFS_ENS(), time, variable, member=[3, 4])
  • Ensemble sources follow EnsembleDataSource or EnsembleForecastSource in earth2studio/data/base.py: a DataSource or ForecastSource whose __call__ and fetch also take an optional member keyword after their other arguments. member takes a label, a list of labels or a MemberArray, as time and variable take a value, list or array. Given, even as one label, the result has a leading ensemble dimension holding those members in request order; omitted, the source returns the member it was built with, without the dimension, so an ensemble source still serves every DataSource or ForecastSource caller. prep_member_inputs normalizes the keyword.
  • The keyword is member and the dimension ensemble, the dimension name runner outputs, IO backends and InferenceOutputSource already use: member selects along ensemble as time and variable select along theirs.
  • A source is an ensemble source when its __call__ signature contains member, mirroring forecast detection. Wrappers that forward requests through *args declare it with a boolean is_ensemble property; RegriddedSource reports its source's. The protocols document the contract and serve type checking; a runtime-checkable protocol checks method names only, so isinstance cannot tell ensemble sources from other sources and detection does not use it.
  • CompositeSource and CompositeForecastSource are ensemble sources when any component is, through is_ensemble. They pass member to those components, which must share member labels, and repeat other components' fields for every member. Without such a component, they reject member.
  • Labels are the source's own: IFS_ENS, IFS_ENS_FX and AIFS_ENS_FX use 0 for the control and 1 and up for perturbed members, GEFS_FX uses gec00 and gep01 to gep30, and InferenceOutputSource uses the stored ensemble coordinate. Any subset, including all members, is requested by listing its labels. Constructor members, such as IFS_ENS(member=k), remain the default for calls without the keyword.
  • fetch_data forwards member to every source call, with qualified labels alike, so a source reduces each member's own samples. It raises if the source returns no ensemble dimension, and selects members in request order. Labels must be distinct; callers repeat members after fetching.

docs.title: Temporal Statistics
docs.text:
fetch_data discovers methods through source.lexicon.TIME_STATISTICS and passes supported qualified labels unchanged. The source aggregates as described in E2S-03_TIME_STATISTICS_SPEC.md:

variables = np.array(["t2m", "t2m:mean:24h", "tp:sum:0h:6h"])

For analysis sources, the source receives valid timestamps time + lead_time and anchors windows to them. For forecast sources, it receives initializations and leads and reduces over leads within each initialization. A source that does not support a requested method raises ValueError before any source calls. Invalid source windows raise before field downloads; fetch_data propagates source errors.

Native adapters use plan_statistics to parse labels and plan sample coordinates, and reduce_statistics to fetch them through a source coroutine and reduce each target's transient sample stack through the registered statistic into the output. Plain variables keep the source's ordinary path. Sources must validate coordinates before fetching and propagate failures. Shared reduction imposes no sampling cadence.

Source results must record native reductions in earth2studio_statistics as specified by the source contract. fetch_data preserves these entries and trusts native capability declarations rather than independently validating each returned metadata entry. Duplicate normalized quantities are rejected before any source calls. Raw backend identifiers containing :: pass through without statistic parsing. Metadata does not record delta_t: source sampling may vary within a window.

Wrappers forward qualified labels. RegriddedSource passes them to its source and regrids the reduced field. The composites route a label by its base name, the text before the first :, so a component providing t2m also receives t2m:mean:24h. Native capability discovery unwraps RegriddedSource and takes the intersection of component methods for composites. A method must therefore be supported by every component to be requested through fetch_data.

docs.title: Output Contract
docs.text:
• Return one xr.DataArray, ordered as [time, lead_time, variable, ...], with remaining source dimensions retained. Lead coordinates use nanosecond precision. With member, a leading ensemble dimension comes first, labeled by the requested members in order.
  • Without a regridder, preserve source spatial coordinates, auxiliary geometry, array name, and source attributes. Do not infer a grid, reconstruct grid metadata, or relabel geometry.
  • With a regridder, spatial coordinates and grid metadata follow its target grid under R3 and R4; other coordinates and attributes are preserved.
  • Preserve the earth2studio_statistics the source records, including metadata for unqualified source variables that are already aggregated.
  • Remove coordinate-signature markers earth2studio_kind, earth2studio_schema_version, and earth2studio_dynamic_dims from the field.
  • Return NumPy-backed values on CPU and CuPy-backed values on the selected CUDA device. Device conversion occurs after fetching, and before regridding.

The former (tensor, coords) return and legacy switch are removed. Consumers access field.data and field.coords; tensor-based consumers can explicitly use prep_data_array.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
Given an analysis source supporting t2m:mean:24h:

field = fetch_data(
    source,
    time=np.array([np.datetime64("2024-01-02T00")]),
    variable=np.array(["t2m", "t2m:mean:24h"]),
    lead_time=np.array([np.timedelta64(0, "h")]),
)

The output contains the instantaneous field and preceding-day mean on the source grid. A six-hourly analysis source averages valid times -18 through 0 hours. For GFS_FX, request a lead of at least 23 hours for this trailing window: at lead 24h, hourly samples are leads 1 through 24h of the same initialization. A trailing window at lead zero is rejected because its required leads are negative.

docs.title: Deferred Work and Verification
docs.text:
Bounds selection, a single coordinate-system request object, and fetch-plan caching are outside this contract. Native reduction is described in the time-statistics spec.

Tests must cover both source types, multiple initializations and leads, mixed instantaneous/statistical labels forwarded unchanged, rejection of unsupported statistics and duplicate quantities, output metadata, native spatial geometry, CPU/CUDA placement, regridding after reduction, compositions forwarding qualified labels, sources returning device arrays, and ensemble members through both source types, temporal statistics, RegriddedSource and the composites. Source aggregation is tested with the shared helper and with each source that supports statistics. The fetch regressions live in test/data/test_fetch_data_xarray.py and test/data/test_data_utils.py, member selection by each ensemble source in its own test file, with regridders in test/grids/test_regrid.py and window semantics in test/utils/test_time_statistics.py.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text:
Define prognostic and diagnostic coordinate, interface, iterator, hook, ownership, RNG and domain-selection semantics for model-independent execution.

This document is the source of truth for the model contract. Prognostic models follow the explicit-state protocol in Model Interface: wrappers implement initialize and step, and may delegate explicit __call__/create_iterator methods to private PrognosticMixin helpers. Where wrappers or the checker do not match yet, this spec governs and Migration lists the gap.

earth2studio.models.conformance checks the rules below and reports their identifiers. Model tests cover execution, batching, metadata, hooks, ownership and checkpoint continuation. DA's companion interfaces are defined in earth2studio/models/da/base.py and the DA user guide; see Open Questions for remaining generic DA planning concerns.

docs.title: Coordinate Systems
docs.text:
CoordinateSystem is an xarray.DataArray created by coord_array() that stores only shape and dtype, never field values, even when every dimension is concrete. Read labels from .coords, order from .dims and lengths from .sizes; field .values are unsupported. Dimension and auxiliary coordinate arrays still occupy memory.

input_coords() is a declaration. Dynamic dimensions form an explicitly marked, zero-sized leading prefix (earth2studio_dynamic_dims). Any model may declare them, under any name (batch, time or model-specific axes); this is not a regional/global distinction. All other dimensions, labels, auxiliary coordinates and declared grid/CRS/statistics metadata must match. Concrete inputs may have any leading batch dimensions, or none. Fixed trailing dimension order is authoritative, and a zero-sized fixed dimension is not a wildcard. Resolve multiple dynamic dimensions together or right to left: concretizing time in (batch, time, ...) keeps batch dynamic, but concretizing only batch leaves a non-leading wildcard and is rejected. Dimensions are never silently reordered, and wildcards never become fixed zero-length axes.

Configure flexible shapes and variable sets on the model instance before querying input_coords(): a model supporting arbitrary crops is configured with its domain, and an observation model with optional channels with its available variables. The declaration then has concrete spatial coordinates and labels, so fetching and output planning are unambiguous. Keep the configuration fixed for a run; changing it requires new signatures and a new fetch/output plan. Models with a selectable spatial domain implement DomainAdaptable (see Domain selection), which returns a new view per region instead of reconfiguring a model in place. Constructors or model-specific setters configure other flexible declarations; a shared variable-selection interface is an open question, not a method callers can rely on. An unresolved wildcard never requests an unspecified region or variable set. Model-specific validation (patch-size multiples, supported channel combinations) supplements the coordinate handshakes.

output_coords(input_coords) validates and resolves outputs without touching field data, so rollouts can be planned before allocation. coord_array_like(input, replacements) preserves leading dimensions, dtype, name, metadata and unaffected coordinates. Replacing lead_time or variable drops dependent auxiliaries (e.g. valid_time, per-variable units); recompute them explicitly if needed. Temporal statistics are declared only in qualified labels such as tp:sum:6h: coord_array() and coord_array_like() derive the earth2studio_statistics attribute from them, recomputing it when variables are replaced. Spatial replacements need coord_array(grid=...) with a new grid definition; coord_array_like() rejects them to prevent stale grid metadata.

docs.title: Grid-backed signatures
docs.text:
Pass a registered name or GridDefinition to coord_array(grid=...) instead of repeating grid axes in each model. The helper attaches grid metadata, earth2studio_crs when the definition has a CRS, and earth2studio_grid_id for registered names. Projected, curvilinear and point signatures include geographic coordinates; HEALPix signatures use index coordinates. Handshakes validate geographic coordinates as well as axes.

  • StormScopeGOES, StormScopeMRMS: checkpoint CurvilinearGrid on y, x; output offsets are added to the final input lead time.
  • StormCastCONUS: cropped ProjectedGrid with registered HRRR CRS on y, x; output advances the final input lead time by one hour.
  • PrecipitationAFNO: registered latlon-0.25deg-south-pole-excluded grid (720 × 1440) on lat, lon; output is tp:sum:6h with derived statistics metadata.

Models declaring relative lead-time history subtract the final input lead time before checking the declared window. Beforehand, lead_time must be an explicit, nonempty 1-D timedelta coordinate without NaT; datetime and numeric labels are rejected. Output planning accepts dynamic declarations and concrete DataArrays without mutating either.
